lead_in: Luke 12:58’s adversary on the way: Augustine says it is the word of God, whose commands we must agree with.

excerpt.text: If you sin, the word of God is your adversary. For example, it is a delight to you perchance to be drunken; it says to you, Do it not. . . . It is the adversary of your will, till it become the author of your salvation. O how goodly, how useful an adversary! It does not seek our will, but our advantage. It is our adversary, as long as we are our own adversaries. As long as you are your own enemy, you have the word of God your enemy; be your own friend, and you are in agreement with it. You shall do no murder; give ear, and you have agreed with it.
excerpt.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 59 on the New Testament (Ben. 109), §3, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6
